Revised event participation fees are intended to strengthen the financial foundation for continued investment in coaching and services

TOKYO, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- LEIFRAS Co., Ltd. (Nasdaq: LFS) (the "Company" or "Leifras"), a sports and social business company dedicated to youth sports and community engagement, and a leading operator of children's sports schools and school club activity support businesses in Japan, today announced that it is working to enhance the value of coaching and services at its sports schools and strengthen profitability through event participation fee changes that have already been implemented.

By strengthening its financial foundation for continued investment in coaching and support for members, the Company aims to enhance its services to children and achieve sustainable growth.

1. Enhancing the Value of Leifras' Distinctive Sports School Coaching and Services

In addition to teaching sports skills, the Company emphasizes helping children develop non-cognitive skills such as courtesy, cooperation, and independence.

Drawing on its experience in coaching and program operations, the Company plans to introduce new services to improve day-to-day coaching and support for its members. It aims to build sports schools where children enjoy participating and see their own progress, and where parents and guardians see the value of continued participation.

The Company will disclose further details and the expected launch timeline for the new services once preparations are complete.

2. Strengthening the Financial Foundation Through Event Fee Changes Already in Effect

The Company has already increased participation fees for certain events offered to sports school members, with adjustments determined on an event-by-event basis. It seeks to give children opportunities to gain new experiences through these events and to improve the profitability of event operations.

By combining the event fee changes with operating expense management, the Company aims to improve profitability in its existing business and strengthen the financial foundation for continued investment in coaching and services.

The Company will assess the financial effects of the changes based on factors including event attendance, revenue, and operating expenses.

3. Outlook

To support investment in new services while improving profitability, the Company plans to manage implementation and operating costs and consider improvements to its operating and procurement practices.

While maintaining the resources and procedures needed for coaching and safety, the Company will assess the costs and benefits of each initiative with the aim of delivering services reliably and improving operational efficiency.

The impact of the event participation fee changes on revenue and profit will depend on factors including attendance, the events held and how they are run, and operating expenses. The Company will assess the financial impact of investments in new services and future collaboration as those initiatives take shape. This release does not announce any confirmed increases in revenue or profit or any upward revision to the Company's financial forecasts.

The Company will disclose relevant developments as appropriate.

Exploring Collaboration with OLI in Sports and Education

Building on the mutual understanding developed through its prior collaboration with Oriental Land Innovations Co., Ltd. ("OLI"), the Company will work with OLI to explore ways to benefit children through sports and education.

The two companies will evaluate whether new opportunities leveraging Leifras' experience in sports education and sports school operations could form the basis of new businesses.

The Company will announce specific collaborative initiatives when they are ready to be disclosed, following review and agreement by both companies.

About LEIFRAS Co., Ltd.

Headquartered in Tokyo, Leifras is a sports and social business company dedicated to youth sports and community engagement. The Company primarily provides services related to the organization and operations of sports schools and sports events for children. Leifras was recognized as Japan's largest operator of children's sports schools in terms of both membership and number of schools, as well as the leading provider of school club activity support in terms of the number of contracted schools, according to Tokyo Shoko Research as of December 2025. The Company's approach to sports education emphasizes the development of non-cognitive skills, following the teaching principle "acknowledge, praise, encourage, and motivate." Its holistic approach integrates physical and mental development. Building on its experience and expertise in sports education, Leifras also operates a social business that supports school club activities, provides sports therapy for children with developmental disabilities, and offers exercise programs for the elderly. As of June 30, 2026, the Company supported 2,224 club activities at 478 schools.

For more information, please visit the Company's website: https://ir.leifras.co.jp/.

DONGGUAN, China, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Dogness (International) Corporation ("Dogness" or the "Company") (NASDAQ: DOGZ), a developer and manufacturer of a comprehensive line of Dogness-branded, OEM and private-label pet products, announced that it showcased its new AI-powered smart pet feeders, alongside its established pet product portfolio, at the 30th China International Pet Show (CIPS 2026), held from November 12 to 15 in Guangzhou, China. The exhibition underscores the Company's continued advancement of its AI-driven smart pet care strategy and its global distribution. Through its distribution network across 35 countries and regions, Dogness aims to commercialize its AI-powered pet products and capture new growth opportunities in the smart pet care industry.

Extensive Global Distribution Network Supports AI Product Commercialization

Dogness's channel network now covers 35 countries and regions worldwide. It sells through global retailers and specialized pet channels including Walmart, Costco, Petco and Pet Valu, online platforms such as Amazon and Chewy, as well as brand and industry partners like Velcro. This broad network and the Company's long-standing relationships provide a foundation for presenting products, gathering market feedback and exploring new collaborations. They also support Dogness's efforts to introduce its new AI products to different markets and adapt its product portfolio to local needs, strengthening its relationships with major international retailers.

Driving AI Innovation in Smart Pet Care Through a Structured Matrix of AI Products

While strengthening its established pet supplies business, Dogness continues to expand the development and production of AI-enabled pet products. The Company continues to invest in R&D for intelligent functions and products designed for specific pet care needs, pursuing a two-track approach that combines an established product foundation with continued AI innovation.

  • New AI Products: Advancing the AI Strategy through Smart Feeding

At CIPS 2026, Dogness showcased the F01B and F10B AI feeders, allowing attendees to explore smart feeding and scenario-based interaction features through hands-on demonstrations. The 3.6-liter F10B, built with Google Gemini, features a high-definition night-vision camera and AI-powered behavior recognition that alerts owners to unusual activity through the Dogness mobile app. The F01B offers a larger 8-liter capacity in a distinct design. AI feeders are an important entry point within the Company's expanding portfolio of AI pet products. Dogness continues to invest in R&D and refine products around real-world pet care needs, advancing the application of AI capabilities in everyday feeding scenarios.

More importantly, Dogness's AI strategy is not a collection of standalone devices but a scenario-driven product matrix. Its technical strengths are reflected in three areas: first, scenario-based interaction capabilities developed around high-frequency pet care scenarios including feeding, interaction and location tracking; second, integrated hardware-software-scenario design that enables AI features to deliver a seamless user experience throughout real-world usage journeys; and third, sustained R&D and iteration capabilities, underpinned by the Company's continued investment in intelligent function development and scenario-based product pipeline reserves. AI feeders serve as the primary entry point, as the product matrix extends into location-tracking use cases, with AI-enabled water fountains in the pipeline to form a multi-scenario AI product matrix covering feeding, hydration and location tracking.

  • Established Product Portfolio as a Robust Foundation for AI-Driven Growth

At CIPS 2026, Dogness also presented quick-release pet leashes, the slow-recovery R06 retractable leash, paw cleaner cups, training mats and reflective collars, covering everyday walking, cleaning, training and visibility needs.

The established portfolio delivers four key pillars supporting Dogness's AI product development: an established customer base and repeat-purchase relationships that create a natural on-ramp for AI products; brand recognition that lowers market education costs for new AI offerings; an integrated, in-house supply chain covering design and R&D, material sourcing, manufacturing and quality control, which supports production of AI products with consistent quality and effective cost control; and existing sales channels, including distributor networks, retail outlets and e-commerce operations, to support the distribution and promotion of AI products.

Furthermore, Dogness's traditional and AI businesses unlock opportunities for cross-selling and mutual promotion. Channel credibility and user relationships built through its established product lineup help AI products gain market traction. In turn, AI products elevate the brand's technological positioning and customer value, reinforcing the established product portfolio. As such, Dogness has built a growth framework wherein its established product portfolio stabilizes the core business and its structured AI product matrix is intended to drive incremental growth.

Silong Chen, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Dogness, commented: "CIPS 2026 enables us to leverage our well-established worldwide sales network and customer base, supported by end-to-end R&D and manufacturing systems, to further advance our strategic transformation from a traditional global pet products manufacturer into a global AI-powered smart pet care technology company, and accelerate the global commercialization of AI-powered pet products."

About Dogness

Dogness (International) Corporation was founded in 2003 from the belief that dogs and cats are important, well-loved family members. Through its smart products, hygiene products, health and wellness products, and leash products, Dogness' technology simplifies pet lifestyles and enhances the relationship between pets and pet caregivers. The Company ensures industry-leading quality through its fully integrated vertical supply chain and world-class research and development capabilities, which have resulted in over 200 patents and patents pending. Dogness products reach families worldwide through global chain stores and distributors. For more information, please visit: ir.dogness.com.

Reinforcing Long-Term Commitment to the Growth of FFR and filed a Schedule 14C with the Securities and Exchange Commission

LOS ANGELES, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem Inc. (NASDAQ: FFR) ("FFR" or the "Company"), a U.S.-based Embodied AI ("EAI") robotics company, today announced it had filed a preliminary Schedule 14C with the Securities and Exchange Commission, which includes pro forma financial information for the acquired robotics business, as well as additional disclosures related to FFR's acquisition of the robotics business of Faraday Future (NASDAQ: FFAI), including transaction details, ownership structure, and other relevant information for stockholders and investors, marking the completion of all material matters required of both parties post deal closing.

As of November 25, 2026, FFAI beneficially owned approximately 14.7 million shares of FFR common stock, representing approximately 53% of FFR's 27.7 million shares currently outstanding. Following the issuance of shares contemplated by FFR's acquisition of the robotics business, FFAI is expected to own approximately 80.1 million shares, or approximately 75% of FFR's anticipated 106.2 million outstanding shares. All newly issued FFR shares received by FFAI in the transaction are subject to an 18‑month lock-up period. Based on FFR's closing market price on November 25, 2026, the implied value of FFAI's expected ownership position would be approximately $41 million.

The holding reflects Faraday Future's continued commitment to supporting the development of the FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem and aligns FFAI's interests with those of FFR stockholders as the company advances the commercialization of its robotics, AI, and intelligent automation solutions.

"FFAI's substantial ownership position reflects its continuing strategic alignment with FFR," said YT Jia, Global CEO of FFAI and FFR. "We believe FFR is uniquely positioned at the intersection of artificial intelligence and robotics, with a growing portfolio of technologies, products, strategic partnerships, and commercialization initiatives designed to create long-term shareholder value."

FFR has continued to expand its robotics ecosystem through advancements across its key business pillars, including Physical AI Devices, the Physical AI Brain and Developer Platform, Industry Productivity Solutions, and the Physical AI Data Factory. The company has also been pursuing commercialization opportunities across enterprise, education, service, and industrial applications.

FFR's strategy is supported by several key factors:

  • Growth in strategic partnerships and commercial deployments;
  • Increasing opportunities to monetize robotics solutions in K-12 education sector, security and surveillance among others; and

FFAI will continue to evaluate opportunities to further support FFR's strategic initiatives, subject to market conditions, corporate requirements, and applicable regulations.

Shares now trade on the TSX Venture Exchange, the OTCQB Venture Market and the Frankfurt Stock Exchange as TruSilver advances drilling at its Sturgis-Walton Silver Project in Nova Scotia

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 27, 2026) - TruSilver Metals Corp. (TSXV: TAG) (OTCQB: TAGMF) (FSE: XJ10) ("TruSilver" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that its common shares have been approved for trading on the OTCQB® Venture Market, operated by OTC Markets Group Inc., and commenced trading under the symbol "TAGMF" on November 27, 2026. The Company's common shares will continue to trade on the TSX Venture Exchange under the symbol "TAG".

The OTCQB is a U.S. trading venue for entrepreneurial and development-stage companies. To qualify, companies must be current in their reporting and pass an annual verification and management certification process. The listing gives U.S. investors a simple way to buy and hold TruSilver shares through their existing brokerage accounts, in U.S. dollars and during U.S. market hours.

Highlights

  • Three markets in one month. TruSilver began trading on the TSX Venture Exchange on October 27, 2026, on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange on November 10, 2026 (FSE: XJ10; WKN: A42QTR), and now on the OTCQB.

  • Broader investor reach. The OTCQB listing opens TruSilver to U.S. retail and institutional investors, alongside its existing Canadian and European shareholder base.

  • Drilling at Sturgis-Walton. TruSilver's planned 2026/27 diamond drilling program of approximately 3,500 metres across five holes is commencing with hole ST-26-01A at its 100%-owned Sturgis-Walton Silver Project, adjacent to the historic Walton Mine.

Michael Gross, President and Chief Executive Officer of TruSilver, commented:

"Adding the OTCQB means investors in Canada, Europe and the United States can now own TruSilver on a market close to home. The U.S. has one of the deepest pools of capital for silver and precious-metals explorers anywhere, and we want those investors following our story from the start. That story is about to be tested with the drill. Sturgis-Walton sits next to one of the historic highest-grade silver mines in Nova Scotia's history, and our geophysics points to a target at depth that has never been properly drilled. Over the coming months our job is simple: drill it, report what we find, and keep our shareholders informed every step of the way."

U.S. investors can find current financial disclosure and Real-Time Level 2 quotes for the Company on www.otcmarkets.com. Canadian disclosure documents, including the Company's filing statement dated October 15, 2026 and the independent NI 43-101 technical report on the Sturgis-Walton Silver Project effective October 7, 2026, are available under the Company's profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca.

About TruSilver Metals Corp.

TruSilver Metals Corp. owns 100% of the Sturgis-Walton Silver Project in Hants County, Nova Scotia, free of a net smelter return royalty, adjacent to the historic Walton Mine, a past barite producer and silver-rich lead-zinc-copper mine, where historical sources report mined ore head grades of 350-933 g/t silver (Ag).¹ TruSilver is commencing drilling of hole ST-26-01A, the first hole of its 2026/27 drill program, aimed squarely at the Sturgis Target: a large, dense and electrically conductive body approximately 1.5 km south of the Walton Mine. The Sturgis Target is where five years of magnetic, audio-magnetotelluric (AMT) and gravity surveys, drilling and 3D modelling converge. The Company's working hypothesis, which this program is designed to test, is that the Sturgis Target may represent a somewhat deeper and along-strike part of the same mineralizing system that formed the Walton Mine. A drilling permit is in place. TruSilver's 2023 hole, ST-23-001 (collared approximately 850 m from the mine), was drilled between the Walton Mine and the newer Sturgis Target, and returned 48.8 g/t silver and 0.19% copper over 19.0 metres in the Macumber Formation, the rock unit that hosted mineralization at the Walton Mine, potentially indicating distal lower-grade mineralization between the two zones.² In late 2025, Rio Tinto Exploration Canada Inc. staked all open mineral claims in the Minas sub-basin, comprising 2,363 claims under 30 exploration licences, surrounding the Sturgis-Walton Silver Project. Rio Tinto is not affiliated with TruSilver, and its activities are not indicative of mineralization on TruSilver's property.

TruSilver's team combines decades of exploration, mine-development and capital-markets experience, with current or former lead technical and board roles at IAMGOLD, Noranda-Falconbridge, Glencore, Sherritt International and Sibanye-Stillwater. Team members contributed to the discovery or acquisition of over 30 million ounces of gold and led the completion and initial ramp-up of a US$7 billion nickel project.

For more information and to sign up for news releases, visit www.TruSilverMetals.com.

¹ Historical information, as summarized in the Technical Report. Source: Nova Scotia Department of Natural Resources Mineral Inventory files (O'Reilly, 2007; Boyd and Cole, 1979). The silver grades are a range of historical head grades reported for ore mined at the Walton Mine, not a single verified average production grade. Neither the Technical Report's author nor TruSilver's Qualified Person has independently verified these historical production figures, and they should not be relied upon. The Walton Mine is not owned by TruSilver, and mineralization on adjacent properties is not necessarily indicative of mineralization on TruSilver's property. No mineral resource has been estimated.

² Drilled length; true width unknown; no formal QA/QC.

At launch, developers will be able to use data from past agent runs to compare commercial cloud models, Apple's on-device foundation models and models running on Apple's Private Cloud Compute, and open-weight models hosted on private or sovereign infrastructure.

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 27, 2026) - Railtown AI Technologies Inc. (CSE: RAIL) (OTCQB: RLAIF) ("Railtown" or the "Company") today announced new on-demand model evaluation capabilities that use data captured from actual agent runs to compare alternative AI models. The technology extends Railtown's agent observability capabilities and helps developers and enterprises assess whether a lower-cost model or a different deployment environment can meet an application's quality and reliability requirements.

Evaluating Models Against Real Application Workloads

Railtown's agent observability technology can run locally or through its Conductr cloud platform, giving developers visibility into agent execution across development and production environments. The new capabilities use historical execution data to evaluate alternative models against real application workloads.

Developers can use these evaluations to identify tasks that may run on smaller, more efficient models, assess whether suitable workloads can move to a device or privately controlled infrastructure, and reduce reliance on any one provider. As new models become available, teams can revisit model choices throughout an application's life.

Evaluating Models in Apple's AI Ecosystem

Combining the new evaluation capabilities with Railtown's open-source Railtracks Swift Agent Development Kit (ADK) and agent observability gives Apple developers a way to assess which workloads could run on Apple's on-device foundation models or on a model running on Apple's Private Cloud Compute, where available.

Moving suitable tasks to an on-device model can reduce external inference costs, keep those model requests on the device and enable offline functionality where supported. Eligible developers can also evaluate Apple's cloud-hosted model for tasks that need more reasoning capacity or a larger context window.

"Developers should be able to look at the work their agents already do and ask where a smaller model can deliver the quality they need," said Marwan Haddad, CTO and Co-Founder of Railtown AI. "For an Apple developer, that might mean moving part of a workflow onto the device. For an enterprise, it might mean running a model on infrastructure it controls. In both cases, the decision starts with data from the application itself."

Supporting Private and Sovereign AI Deployments

Enterprises and governments seeking greater control over sensitive data and intellectual property can use the technology to assess whether open-weight models running on infrastructure they control meet the requirements of existing applications.

In Canada, Railtown sees an opportunity to complement investment in sovereign AI infrastructure by helping organizations identify which workloads can move to domestically controlled computing environments and what changes those workloads may require.

The new capabilities extend Railtown's agent development tools, which include the open-source Railtracks Swift and Python ADKs, knowledge retrieval technology, agent observability and the Conductr platform. The Company is also exploring ways to build on its observability and evaluation technology to help developers optimize prompts and agent workflows.

Railtown expects to make the evaluation capabilities available to developers soon and plans to publish a technical blog demonstrating how to use them.

About Railtown AI Technologies Inc.

Railtown AI Technologies Inc. is an AI technology company developing tools and infrastructure that enable developers and organizations to build, deploy, manage and observe AI-powered applications and agents.

Its technology includes Conductr, an agentic AI orchestration, deployment and observability platform; Railengine, its knowledge and data infrastructure; and Railtracks, its open-source Agent Development Kit.

Railtown is focused on simplifying the development and operation of agentic applications while supporting organizations seeking flexible, secure and scalable AI solutions.

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 27, 2026) - The Precision Peptide Company (CSE: BPC) (OTCQB: PNGAF) (the "Company"), a publicly traded wellness company focused on advanced peptide formulations and delivery systems, today announced that its tirzepatide and GLP3 transdermal patches have each passed formal U.S. testing and that it has ordered 20,000 units of each from its exclusive U.S. manufacturer. They are the third and fourth patches in the Company's needle-free line to reach a commercial production order, following BPC-157 and Thymosin Alpha-1, and the Company is targeting a full needle-free lineup on sale by the first quarter of 2027, up from the single patch on sale today.

The tirzepatide patch was announced as under development on August 19, 2026 and entered formal U.S. testing on October 13, 2026. The GLP3 patch entered development on October 20, 2026. Both are in the Company's metabolic and weight-management category, and both have now passed the same U.S. testing stage that the Company's BPC-157 and Thymosin Alpha-1 ("TA1") patches passed before their own production orders.

100% Tested and Manufactured in the United States

Every patch in the line follows the same production and testing process: formulated in the United States, tested in the United States by an independent laboratory, produced in the United States, then released. The first patch through that process, The Recovery Patch (BPC-157), recorded 95.5% chromatographic purity and a quantified 2.02 mg dose per patch in independent laboratory testing, exceeding the 95% threshold widely used as the benchmark for high-purity peptide products.

TA1 followed with a 20,000-unit order at 2 mg per patch. Tirzepatide and GLP3 have now cleared the same stage. All four formulations are produced by one U.S. manufacturer solely for the Company under the exclusive manufacturing rights announced on October 22, 2026, so that one testing standard and one production standard apply across the whole line.

The Needle-Free Line at a Glance

BPC-157 (The Recovery Patch)On saleIndependent U.S. laboratory testing recorded 95.5% purity and a 2.02 mg dose per patch (May 19, 2026); approximately 20,000 units received July 2026 (July 14, 2026); available at store.precisionpep.co
Thymosin Alpha-1 (TA1)In productionEntered formal U.S. testing September 2026; 20,000 units ordered October 2026 at 2 mg per patch, delivery expected January 2027 (October 7, 2026)
TirzepatideIn productionDevelopment announced August 2026 (August 19, 2026); entered formal U.S. testing October 2026 (October 13, 2026); testing passed; 20,000 units ordered November 2026
GLP3In productionDevelopment announced October 2026 (October 20, 2026); formal U.S. testing passed; 20,000 units ordered November 2026

A Full Line by Q1 2027

The Recovery Patch, on sale since July 2026, was the first product in the Company's needle-free range. With 20,000-unit orders now placed for TA1, tirzepatide and GLP3, the Company is targeting a full needle-free lineup on sale by the end of the first quarter of 2027. Each patch will be sold through the Company's direct-to-consumer website and its wholesale program for clinics, medical spas, gyms and retailers in all 50 U.S. states.

No Needle, No Mixing, No Refrigeration

Injectable peptides, including the Company's own prescription vials, are typically supplied as a powder that must be mixed with sterile water, measured into a syringe, injected and kept refrigerated. The Company's patches remove those steps. The Company's patches are applied to the skin, and each patch delivers a pre-measured dose: no needle, no mixing, no measuring, no cold storage. Discreet, portable and consistent from one dose to the next, they fit into a daily routine and open peptides to the many people who were interested but prefer not to use a syringe.

Market Context

Tirzepatide and GLP3 are the Company's two patches in the metabolic and weight-management category. The global GLP-1 market was valued at approximately US$66 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach US$185.3 billion by 2033,[2,3] with injectable delivery accounting for 69.1% of the market in 2025.[2] The broader global peptide therapeutics market was valued at US$56.06 billion in 2026 and is projected to reach US$87.21 billion by 2035, with North America the largest regional market.[1] The Company believes that U.S.-based development, testing and manufacturing, combined with a needle-free format, position it to compete as those markets expand.

The foregoing market data is provided as context for the Company's product development activities and should not be construed as a projection of the Company's future revenue or market share.

Pratap Sandhu, CEO of The Precision Peptide Company, commented:

"We are making significant progress in turning our needle-free patches into a commercial product portfolio. In just four months, we have grown from one patch on sale to three additional patches ordered for production, including 40,000 tirzepatide and GLP3 patches following successful U.S. testing. Our exclusive U.S. manufacturing partnership gives us a strong foundation to expand production while maintaining consistent quality standards. We are targeting commercial availability of all four patches by March 2027, with MOTS-c now also in development as our fifth. Our priority is clear: accelerate commercialization, expand our product portfolio and establish The Precision Peptide Company as a leader in needle-free peptide delivery."

The proceeds from the Loan will be primarily used to repay the Company's C$700,000 principal amount convertible note issued to Texas Critical Minerals, LLC ("TCM") in October 2024, which matured on October 25, 2025, together with all accrued interest.

The principal amount of the Loan will mature and be repayable in full on the date which is three years from closing, and will be convertible into common shares at the option of the Lenders at any time prior to the close of business on the maturity date at a conversion price of $0.30 per share. The principal amount of the Loan will bear interest at 8.5% per annum, payable annually on December 31, commencing December 31, 2027. Subject to the approval of the TSX Venture Exchange ("TSXV"), Search will have the option to pay interest in common shares in lieu of cash at the market price for the common shares at the time the interest becomes payable. Any conversion that would result in a Lender becoming a Control Person (as defined in the policies of the TSXV) will be subject to prior TSXV approval, including shareholder approval. The Loan will be secured by a pledge of the shares of the Company's subsidiaries Alterra Resources Inc. and 86857 Newfoundland & Labrador Inc., together with guarantees and personal property security granted by those subsidiaries.

Upon completion, the transaction is expected to:

  • Lower interest rate costs: reduce the interest rate on the TCM note being repaid from 15% to 8.5%;
  • Reduce TCM's claims: resolve the claim TCM has filed against the Company relating to the note, one of three claims filed by TCM against the Company as disclosed in the Company's financial statements. With respect to the two remaining claims, the Company continues to dispute the amounts alleged to be owing, believes it has credible defences, and intends to defend its position while remaining focused on advancing its core projects and protecting shareholder interests; and
  • Improve working capital: remove past-due debt owed to TCM from the Company's working capital deficit, subject to final accounting treatment, by extending the maturity dates for the Company's debt and treating such liability as non-current, and provide funds for general working capital.

Jonathan Beigle, Chief Executive Officer and Director of Search Minerals, commented: "We appreciate the continued support of our largest shareholders. This financing allows us to repay the TCM note, lower our interest costs and extend maturities. This will allow us to focus all of our effort on advancing our projects for the benefit of all shareholders."

Closing of the transaction is expected in mid-December, 2026. The Term Sheet is a preliminary binding agreement; completion of the transaction remains subject to, among other things, negotiation and execution of definitive documentation, approval of the Company's Board of Directors and a special committee of independent directors, acceptance of the TSXV, and satisfaction of customary conditions. There can be no assurance that the transaction will be completed on the terms described or at all.

NEW YORK CITY, NY / ACCESS Newswire / November 27, 2026 / SMX, a pioneer in molecular marking and digital material authentication technology, was featured this week in an opinion piece published by The Denver Post examining the need for greater transparency, traceability and accountability in Colorado's evolving recycling economy.

The article, titled "Colorado Has Built a Recycling Framework. Now It Needs Proof," was published on November 23 and addresses one of the most pressing challenges facing states as they implement ambitious environmental legislation: establishing credible proof that materials are being recycled and returned to the economy.

Colorado has made significant strides in advancing sustainability through its Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) legislation, which places greater accountability on manufacturers and producers for the lifecycle of packaging materials. The next opportunity lies in establishing the technological infrastructure to support those policies.

SMX's proprietary molecular marking technology and Digital Material Passport Platform (DMPP) are designed to address this challenge by giving physical materials a persistent identity linked to a secure digital record. The technology enables businesses to authenticate materials, establish chain of custody, document recycled content and create audit-ready records throughout the supply chain.

By making recycled materials identifiable and certifiable, SMX aims to help manufacturers, recyclers and regulators move beyond traditional reporting methods toward a system grounded in scientific proof.

The Denver Post placement comes as the national conversation around recycling increasingly shifts from environmental commitments to measurable outcomes, regulatory compliance and the economic competitiveness of recycled materials.

SMX's technology is designed to help bridge the gap between legislative ambition and industrial execution, providing the tools necessary to build a more transparent, accountable and commercially viable circular economy.

The Denver Post article is one in a series of recent media profiles about SMX. Other stories have run in Tech Crunch, Benzinga, Forbes, the Boston Herald, the Chicago Tribune, Los Angeles Tribune, Miami Herald, Time, and Rolling Stone, among others.

Provides Drilling Update on its Flagship Elida Porphyry Cu-Mo-Ag Deposit

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 27, 2026) - Element 29 Resources Inc. (TSXV: ECU) (OTCQX: EMTRF) (BVL: ECU) ("Element 29" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that it has signed a three-year surface Access Agreement with the host community at its Flor de Cobre Porphyry Copper-Molybdenum ("Cu-Mo") Project ("Flor de Cobre" or the "Project") in southern Perú (Figure 1). This agreement, which expires November 5, 2029, secures long-term access to Flor de Cobre and marks a significant milestone for the Company.

Richard Osmond, President and CEO, commented: "The successful signing of the community Access Agreement underscores the strength of our local relationships and commitment to advancing our projects in close collaboration with rightsholders. We remain focused on progressing Flor de Cobre in a responsible and mutually beneficial manner as we work to unlock its full exploration potential. We are grateful to the community for their ongoing support and partnership."

The signing of the Access Agreement with the host Indigenous community at Flor de Cobre satisfies the final outstanding community-access requirement associated with the Company's application for a Permiso de Inicio de Actividades ("PIA") drilling permit. The PIA application seeks authorization to commence exploration drilling covered by the already approved Declaración de Impacto Ambiental ("DIA") environmental certificate, which provides for drilling from up to 40 platforms over a five-year period (see the March 1, 2024 news release).

The Company previously received an exemption from the Consulta Previa ("Prior Consultation") process on October 21, 2024 (see October 31, 2024 news release), following a review by the Peruvian Ministry of Energy and Mines ("MINEM") of the Collective Impacts Report and its assessment of the potential impacts of exploration drilling on the host Indigenous community's lands.

The Company submitted the PIA application to MINEM on November 10, 2026, which remains pending review and final approval.

Elida Drilling Program Update

The ongoing Elida drilling program is being conducted under the 40-platform PIA drill permit approved in July of 2026 (see the July 28, 2026, news release). The Company started the year with two diamond drill rigs, then added a third rig in September and a fourth is scheduled to arrive in early December. The Company has completed 9,292 metres of its planned 10,000-metre 2026 program. Cumulative drilling at Elida now totals 32,699 metres, more than twice the 14,361 metres of drilling used to prepare the 2022 initial pit-constrained Inferred Mineral Resource Estimate ("MRE") ¹.

Elida is accessible year-round for drilling, and the Company plans to continue the program with four rigs for the remainder of 2026 and through 2027. Local assay laboratory turnaround is currently two to four weeks.

Assay Results Pending for Recently Completed Holes

Recently completed holes ELID044 and ELID045 reached depths of 1,812.8 metres and 1,820.6 metres, respectively. Both holes focused on step-out drilling to extend Zone 1 westward and evaluate potential resource expansion beyond the current MRE. They were designed to follow up on the long-mineralized intercepts in ELID033, ELID035 and ELID037, which suggest the potential for stronger Cu-Mo-Ag mineralization at depth and westward toward the contact with the Coastal Batholith (Figure 2).

ELID044 intersected 1,572.9 metres of potassic-altered volcanosedimentary rocks, from 35.1 metres below the bedrock surface to 1,608.0 metres downhole. The interval contains porphyry-related stockwork veining of varying intensity, with disseminated and stringer chalcopyrite-molybdenite mineralization. At 1,608.0 metres, the hole entered a potassic-altered granodiorite intrusion with stockwork veining and disseminated and stringer chalcopyrite-molybdenite mineralization. The granodiorite continued to the end of the hole at 1,812.8 metres, where drilling was shut down due to the depth limitations of the rig.

ELID045 intersected potassic-altered volcanosedimentary rocks, from 78.7 metres below the bedrock surface to 1,245.5 metres downhole. The interval contains stockwork veining, with disseminated and stringer chalcopyrite-molybdenite mineralization. At 1,245.5 metres, the hole intersected 61.2 metres of potassic-altered granodiorite cut by narrow fingers of potassic-altered quartz monzonite porphyry ("QMP"). Both rock types contain stockwork veining with disseminated chalcopyrite-molybdenite mineralization. From 1,306.7 metres, the hole intersected 358.9 metres of potassic-altered QMP, interpreted as an early-intermineral porphyry, with stockwork veining and disseminated and stringer chalcopyrite-molybdenite mineralization. Below this interval, the hole re-entered potassic-altered, locally brecciated volcanosedimentary rocks, with stockwork veining and disseminated and stringer chalcopyrite-molybdenite mineralization. The hole terminated at 1,820.6 metres due to the depth limitations of the rig.

ELID046 was drilled to a depth of 956.2 metres and was the first hole to evaluate Zone 4, a high-priority target immediately west of Zone 1 within the Elida porphyry cluster. Zone 4 hosts a mineralized porphyry stock emplaced along the contact between the Coastal Batholith and volcanosedimentary rocks. The stock and host rocks exhibit phyllic alteration overprinting earlier potassic alteration, as well as visible copper-oxide staining and anomalous Cu-Mo rock geochemistry. These features support the target's prospectivity for Cu-Mo-Ag mineralization. The hole intersected a 395.9-metre interval of phyllic-overprinted, potassic-altered QMP beginning at 197.8 metres downhole. The QMP is interpreted as a potassic-altered intermineral porphyry intrusion, with stockwork veining containing disseminated and stringer chalcopyrite-molybdenite mineralization. Locally, chalcocite and covellite occur as disseminations and rimming chalcopyrite and pyrite.

True widths are unknown, and assay results for all three holes are pending.

Metallurgical Test Work

In parallel, the Company is advancing the resource modelling and metallurgical test work with Synectiq Inc., as announced on May 7, 2026. The test work is designed to characterize the principal ore types, evaluate copper, molybdenum, and silver recoveries, and assess concentrate quality. The results are intended to support assumptions for an updated mineral resource estimate and future technical studies.

About Flor de Cobre

Flor de Cobre is located 35 kilometres southeast of Arequipa and straddles the border between the Departments of Arequipa and Moquegua, the Provinces of Arequipa and General Sanchez Cerro, and the Districts of Polobaya and La Capilla.

The property is comprised of eleven mining concessions for a total of 2,984.4 hectares ("ha") which are 100% owned by the Company's Peruvian subsidiary Candelaria Resources S.A.C. The project is in the Southern Perú Copper Belt, which is host to numerous porphyry Cu-Mo deposits, including the Cerro Verde Cu-Mo mine operated by Freeport-McMoRan2; the Cuajone and Toquepala Cu-Mo mines operated by Southern Copper2; and the Quellaveco Cu-Mo mine operated by Anglo American2. Flor de Cobre is 5 kilometres northwest of the Chapi Mine and 26 kilometres southeast of the Cerro Verde Mine (Figure 1).

Flor de Cobre hosts the Atravesado porphyry Cu-Mo target, a classic Andean porphyry system with Cu-Mo mineralization potentially associated with a multi-phase quartz monzonite porphyry complex. Atravesado is characterized by widespread Cu-oxide mineralization and strong surface rock Cu geochemistry associated with lower Cretaceous-aged quartzite and sandstone sedimentary rocks which form the upper part of the Yura Group. These rocks are also cut by several narrow potassic altered quartz monzonite porphyry dykes.

The property is situated at a modest elevation of 2,700 metres with excellent infrastructure for future mine development and is accessible along paved and maintained unpaved roads from the hub-city of Arequipa.

Initial order forms part of a previously announced commercial framework from January 2025 with a potential of up to $2.1 million; follows successful completion of end-customer validation, for autonomous drones’ application.

NESS ZIONA, Israel, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Foresight Autonomous Holdings Ltd. (Nasdaq and TASE: FRSX) (“Foresight” or the “Company”), an innovator in 3D perception systems and AI autonomous stacks, today announced that its wholly owned subsidiary, Foresight Intelligent Systems Ltd., has received a conditional and non-binding order from an Indian drone manufacturing company for thermal ScaleCam 3D perception systems. The order is valued at approximately $1.3 million and the systems are intended for integration into autonomous drones for the Indian defense forces.

The order is part of the commercial cooperation framework announced by the Company in January 2025 with a prominent Indian drone manufacturer that is a supplier of the Indian Ministry of Defense. That framework carried previously disclosed commercial potential of up to $2.1 million. The current order follows the successful completion of the validation of Foresight’s thermal ScaleCam 3D perception solution under the agreement.

The order is conditional and remains subject to certain conditions including the successful completion of trials with the Indian Navy, completion of the relevant procurement and commercial negotiation process, and receipt of all required governmental, export-control, and regulatory approvals, where applicable.

Foresight’s 3D perception solution, which uses stereoscopic long-wave infrared technology and integrates internal measurement unit sensors, is designed to maintain robust autonomous drone performances in challenging GPS-denied environments such as dense smoke, poor lighting and high temperatures, enabling the detection of fire source and all object detection while providing real-time information on the drone’s spatial positioning. These capabilities make the solution particularly well-suited for defense unmanned ariel vehicle applications.

“The receipt of this conditional order is an important step forward in our collaboration with our Indian partner and validates the successful completion of the development phase,” said Haim Siboni, Chief Executive Officer of Foresight Intelligent Systems Ltd. “We look forward to progressing through the remaining trials and procurement stages.”

About Foresight
Foresight Autonomous Holdings Ltd. (Nasdaq and TASE: FRSX) is a technology company developing advanced three-dimensional (3D) perception systems, AI autonomous stack, and cellular-based applications. Through its wholly owned subsidiaries, Foresight Intelligent Systems Ltd. (formerly known as Foresight Automotive Ltd.), Foresight Changzhou Automotive Ltd., and Eye-Net Mobile Ltd., Foresight develops both “in-line-of-sight” vision systems and “beyond-line-of-sight” accident-prevention solutions.

Foresight’s 3D perception systems include modules of automatic calibration and dense 3D point cloud that can be applied to different markets such as automotive, defense, autonomous driving, agriculture, heavy industrial equipment, and unmanned aerial vehicles.

Eye-Net Mobile develops next-generation vehicle-to-everything collision prevention solutions and smart automotive systems to enhance road safety and situational awareness for all road users in urban mobility environments. By leveraging cutting-edge artificial intelligence technology, advanced analytics, and existing cellular networks, Eye-Net’s innovative solution suite delivers real-time pre-collision alerts to all road users via smartphones and other smart devices within vehicles.

Thunder Bay, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 27, 2026) - Benton Resources Inc. (TSXV: BEX) ("Benton" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that the Company has acquired a strategic parcel of land consisting of 18 claim units in one mineral licence, contiguous to and within its Dominion land package. The Company has signed a purchase agreement with three arm's-length individuals (the "Vendors") who currently hold the licence. The land parcel sits in the south-central part of Benton's Dominion project and approximately 1.5km SW of Canterra Minerals Corporation's Daniel's Pond VMS deposit (see Figure 1).

Subject to TSX Venture Exchange approval, the Company will make a one-time payment of $12,000 and issue 120,000 shares, which will be allocated equally among the Vendors. The Vendors will retain a 2.0% NSR subject to the right of the Company to purchase back 1.0% for $1.0 million dollars. There were no finders' fees paid in connection with this acquisition.

QP

Stephen House (P.Geo.), Vice President of Exploration for Benton Resources Inc., the 'Qualified Person' under National Instrument 43-101, has approved the scientific and technical disclosure in this news release and prepared or supervised its preparation.

QA/QC Protocols

Core and rock samples, including standards, blanks and duplicates, are submitted to Eastern Analytical Ltd., Springdale, Newfoundland for preparation and analysis. All samples were acquired by saw-cut (channels/drill core) with one-half submitted for assay and one-half retained for reference, or hand (rocks) and delivered, by Benton personnel, in sealed bags, to the Springdale lab, which is an accredited assay lab that conforms to the requirements of ISO/IEC 17025. Samples are analyzed by Au Fire assay @ 30 g + ICP-34 method that delivers a 34-element package utilizing a 200 mg subsample totally dissolved in four acids and analyzed by ICP-OES analytical technique. Overlimits are analyzed using the atomic absorption method, using a 0.200 g to 2.00 g of sample, digested with three acids. All reported assays are uncut. Eastern achieved ISO 17025 accreditation in February 2014 (for more details on the scope of accreditation visit the CALA website). Grab samples are selective in nature and may not represent the average mineralization of a bedrock exposure.
